ops.title: Fleet deadline-budget convention: the budget is a DEFAULT, not a ceiling
ops.body:
daemonkit v0.21 verbs refuse a context with no deadline — `Business.Call` (business.go:249-252), `Business.Close` (:292-295), and `Child.Stop` (child.go:81-84) each check `ctx.Deadline()` and return an error BEFORE doing any work. So an unbounded call site is not a slow path, it is a silently converted no-op: a `Stop` that never terminates a child, a `Close` that never closes.

The fleet-wide fix pattern is cc-notes commit `701f144`. Its `budgeted` helper is:

    if _, stated := ctx.Deadline(); stated {
        return context.WithCancel(ctx)
    }
    return context.WithTimeout(ctx, budget)

RULED 2026-08-03, after a lane checked the commit rather than the paraphrase of it: **the budget is a DEFAULT, not a ceiling.** If the caller stated any deadline — earlier OR later — it survives untouched, and the budget applies only when there is none. Plain `context.WithTimeout(ctx, budget)` is NOT equivalent: it clamps a caller who deliberately asked for longer.

Why default beats ceiling:
1. The case that motivates the whole bug class — a lifetime ctx, `context.Background()`, or `context.WithoutCancel(...)` — carries no deadline at all, so both semantics behave identically there. They diverge only for a caller who explicitly stated a longer deadline.
2. In exactly that case the caller made a deliberate decision, and an entry-point default overriding it is the entry point second-guessing its caller.
3. It is already the fleet's shipped shape. Two repos sharing a helper name with different semantics is worse than either choice.

Each fix carries three properties: a NAMED budget constant per entry point (never a bare literal at the call site — and prefer REUSING an existing well-named settlement constant over minting a near-duplicate); the caller's stated deadline preserved per the rule above; and a one-line source-text contract saying the entry point must hand daemonkit a bounded context. That comment is a non-obvious workaround, one of the few comment exceptions the style guides allow.

TWO TRAPS, both observed live:

- `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` strips the DEADLINE along with cancellation. It is documented to return a context that "returns no Deadline or Err". No upstream budget can survive it, so a `WithoutCancel` handed straight to a daemonkit verb is always a defect. This was cookiesync's bug (internal/daemon/bridge.go:266).
- Never put a deadline on a LIFETIME context. Where a ctx is the run-until-signal gate for a child (e.g. a `signal.NotifyContext` result used as a mount's lifetime), a deadline kills the child on a timer. Derive a bounded ctx per call instead.

A refused verb can also poison a `sync.Once`: cookiesync's `Proc.CloseContext` ran under `closeOnce`, so the refusal latched into `closeErr` and no later correctly-bounded `Close()` could settle it — leaving an orphaned Chrome process against a deleted user-data-dir. Check for once-guards around any site you fix.

SWEEP RESULT (2026-08-03, two-stage checker + independent confirmer across 11 fleet repos): 10 clean — cc-interact, captain-hook, synckit, cc-review, cc-present, reposync, cc-orchestrate, binrun, cc-patch. cookiesync 1 confirmed (fixed, `fc41a72`). fusekit 8 confirmed of 11 flagged.
